title: Minimum Operations to Make a Rotated Palindrome I
approach: Rotations only permute and increments only add, so the two commute and any solution is 'rotate left r times, then increment': cost = r + palcost(rot_r(s)), and only r in [0, n-1] can be optimal. For a fixed rotation the mirrored pairs are independent, and a pair (a,b) costs the CYCLIC distance min((b-a)%26, (a-b)%26) -- meeting at any third letter x costs (x-a)%26 + (x-b)%26, which is 26-d for x below b and d at x=b, so raising one side to the other is always optimal. Try all n rotations: O(n^2), trivial at n <= 2000.

techniques.label: brute-force
techniques.why: n <= 2000 invites enumerating all n rotations and scoring each in O(n)

techniques.label: palindrome
techniques.why: the target condition; cost decomposes over the (i, n-1-i) mirrored pairs

techniques.label: modular-arithmetic
techniques.why: increments wrap z->a, so a pair costs the mod-26 cyclic distance min(d, 26-d), not |a-b|

techniques.label: two-pointers
techniques.why: each rotation is scored by walking inward from both ends; standard palindrome pairing

techniques.label: greedy
techniques.why: REJECTED from patterns: per-pair 'raise the cheaper side' is a closed form over independent subproblems, not an exchange-argument greedy; too weak to earn the label

techniques.label: booth-algorithm
techniques.why: REJECTED: rotations appear, but we need the cost of every rotation, not the lexicographically minimal one

verified: python3 brute force. Exhaustive over all 676 length-2 strings and random length-3/4 strings against a true BFS on the real operation graph (every increment and rotation an edge of weight 1, stop at the first palindrome) -- the BFS assumes nothing about the structure of an optimal solution. Also checked n=5..25 against a semi-brute force that enumerates rotation x independently chosen meeting letter per pair. Statement examples reproduced: "abc" -> 2 (rotate to "bca", then a->b), "yb" -> 3. n=2000 runs in 0.33s.
